director.why: q1 offers the highest expected information at 0.128 bits and models converge on continued fading so near-term r photometry tests it without senior review.

question.text: Brighter in r three days from now than at its last r detection?

risky.text: Brighter than 65 microjansky in r 4 days from now?

payload.rule: Every ZTF g or r measurement taken after this bet was sealed, up to one day past its last forecast, is scored against the forecast, interpolated linearly between days. The question is settled by the first r measurement within a day of its time; a limit above the reference leaves it void.

instrument.why: Detections span 20 days with slow consistent fade and repeatable same-night photometry plus a real PSF-like stamp at high latitude.

theories.argument: The r-only light curve shows a slow ~0.6 mag decline over 20 days from mag 18.6 to 19.3, consistent with a Type II plateau seen at z=0.015 about 34 days after peak. The Type II fit is the best model with chi2 per point of 0.4 and leading weight 0.37, supported by a real PSF-like source offset from its host at high Galactic latitude.

refuted_if.why: A Type II plateau at this redshift cannot fade from ~70 uJy to below 40 uJy in ~5 days without leaving the plateau.

theories.weakest_point: No g-band color and no observed rise or peak leave the early temperature and explosion epoch unconstrained, letting the nearly equal-weight SN Ia model fit the same r-only decline.

theories.argument: The r-band detections fade by about 0.6 mag over 20 days after the fitted peak at day -20, matching a fast-declining Type Ia on the cobalt tail with excellent chi2 per point of 0.24. The fit finds redshift 0.082 with normal color c near -0.03 and x1 near -3, consistent with a subluminous Ia seen as a real off-nucleus point source at high Galactic latitude.

refuted_if.why: A Type Ia at 24 days past peak must continue fading on the tail, so r-band still near 69 microJy would rule out the predicted decline to under 50 microJy.

theories.weakest_point: The inference rests on five r-only detections with no g-band color to confirm the Ia spectral energy distribution and pushes x1 to the extreme fast edge of the model.

theories.argument: The r-band light curve fades ~0.6 mag over 20 days and is fit excellently by a Type Ib/c at z=0.158 peaking 41.5 days ago with chi2 per point 0.21, consistent with a stripped-envelope event on its cobalt tail. The detection is a real PSF-like point source offset from the host at high Galactic latitude, supporting an extragalactic supernova.

refuted_if.why: A 44-day post-peak Ib/c tail must keep fading from ~70 uJy, so a rise to 90 uJy would require rebrightening incompatible with the fit.

theories.weakest_point: The case rests on only five late-tail r-band points with no color information and carries the lowest supernova weight at 0.18.

wording.text: It is unlikely that the object will appear brighter than the set limit four days from now.
